column2: jig dispatcher: runs a subcommand from the version the project pins, else current; changelog and upgrade always run from current; run by hand or by units; results go to stdout
jig which: prints the tree the dispatcher chose for a project; run by hand; result goes to stdout
jig validate: checks the form of a unit prompt or report; run by hand and by units; failures go to stderr, one per line, with the exit code

jig start: checks the preconditions, commits the status line and starts a unit in its worker account; run by the orchestrator; refusals go to stderr, the session's output to ~/ws/reviews/<project>/out/<ID>.txt

jig start, worker part: checks the clone and starts the unit's tmux session and lock; sent over ssh by jig start, or run alone in the worker account; refusals go to stderr, the session's output to ~/ws/reviews/<project>/out/<ID>.txt
lint A: checks comments and docs for private facts; run by make check; results go to stderr
commit-msg hook: checks a commit message and its trailers; run by git on commit, installed by make check; results go to stderr
push-on-token: sets a clone to push on a token file and fetch on its deploy key; run once per clone; results go to the clone's local git config

ci-green: exits 0 when every CI job of a commit succeeded; with --wait <seconds> it waits for every job and every workflow run of the commit to complete, ends at once on a failed job, and gives up with "CI not finished" at the cap; run by a checks row and by jig release prepare; results go to stdout and the exit code
run-mutants: proves each tool's test fails under its seeded break; run by the mutants checks row, not in CI; results go to stdout and the exit code

install: installs one version under the install root, from a clone's committed tree or from a package file of make package, and sets current when it is the newest; run by hand for the bootstrap and by jig upgrade with a downloaded package; results go to stdout and the install root

jig run: checks a block's hash and runs it with bash -l as the person who runs the line; run by hand on the orchestrators' host; output to the terminal and the readback in /srv/jig/out/<project>/<ID>.txt
jigfn: the client functions jigin, jigblock and jigshot; sourced from .bashrc on a person's machine, with JIG_HOST set; results go to the inbox or out/ on the host by scp
jig status: one line per running unit: project, role, tmux, started, k/n, last status; run by the orchestrator or by hand; results go to stdout

jig wait: waits on a running unit with no model, until its report, its end, a dialog, a screen with no change or the timeout, each with its own exit code; run by the orchestrator; the end line, and the screen except for the specwriter account, go to stdout
jig cat: prints a file under a worker account's ~/ws/reviews/<project>/ by ssh, never out/ or transcripts/ of the specwriter account; run by the orchestrator; results go to stdout, refusals to stderr

jig orch: the supervisor of <project>-orch: starts the orchestrator session in tmux and starts it again when it exits (not after 3 exits in 10 minutes), ends a fork of the old session (a process of its account that resumes the old session ID) when the session exits and for 60 s after the restart, announces new files in /srv/jig/in/<project> and /srv/jig/out/<project> into the session, sends "report: <ID> <status>" into the session for each report commit on origin, sends "hourly update" every hour when something changed and otherwise writes an idle line itself, sends "reminder: <item>" once for each dated Open item of impl/orch/state.md whose act-by date has come (at the start and every hour), reports a dialog; run by the orchestrator account with jig orch <project> start|stop|status; results go to ~/ws/reviews/<project>/orch/supervisor.log (the sent reminders in orch/reminded), the tee out/orch.txt and the idle lines in impl/orch/updates.log of the project's -dev clone

jig new: makes a project's directories in the three accounts, conf files, deploy keys, blocks/in/out and checks/<project> (mode 2775) under /srv/jig and the seed repos from templates/new, with the product CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs make check on every push, and writes the block new.sh for the owner's steps; run by the orchestrator with jig new <project>; results go to stdout, the block to /srv/jig/blocks/<project>/new.sh
jig new, account part: makes one account's directories, conf file and deploy keys, never changing a file that exists; sent over ssh by jig new; results go to stdout as made or kept lines
jig close: ends a unit's session, frees its lock, copies its transcripts and commits its end line in status.log; run by the orchestrator; refusals go to stderr, progress to stdout

jig close, worker part: ends one tmux session, frees the lock only when it names that session, copies the unit's transcripts to transcripts/<ID>/<run>/; sent over ssh by jig close; results go to stdout, failures to stderr
jig send: types a one-line correction into a running unit's tmux session and submits it, only when the session shows its input bar; run by the orchestrator; refusals go to stderr, never the screen
jig send, worker part: types the text into one tmux session and submits it, after jig_tmux.py on stdin; sent over ssh by jig send; refusals go to stderr

jig run-check: runs one checks.tsv row of the -dev repo within its time cap, inside a unit's tmux session; run by units; output to ~/ws/reviews/<project>/<ID>-<name>.txt, the exit code to <ID>-<name>.exit beside it; for a row of an account other than the implementer also a copy with the -dev head commit in /srv/jig/checks/<project>/<name>.exit (exit 1 when the copy cannot be written); refusals to stderr

jig report: validates a unit's committed report, checks its commit hashes, fills checks: and context: from the exit files and the context readout, and commits it as "report: <ID>"; run by the orchestrator; refusals go to stderr, the result to stdout
jig report, worker part: lists the unit's exit files in ~/ws/reviews/<project>/; sent over ssh by jig report; the list goes to stdout as JSON

jig batch: runs the units of a batch file one at a time with jig start, jig wait, jig report and jig close, with rows of kind pre-check and review beside the units, and stops on NEEDS ERIC, a failed report, a hold, a dialog, a timeout, a refusal, a must-fix or should-fix finding of a pre-check, a must-fix finding of a review, or a missing findings file, each with its own exit code; run by the orchestrator; one timestamped line per start, report, close and stop goes to stdout
jig hold: sets the hold of a project, /run/jig/hold/<project>, so that jig batch starts no further unit; run by the orchestrator or by hand; the result goes to stdout
jig unhold: clears the hold of a project, so that the next jig batch can start units again; run by the orchestrator or by hand; the result goes to stdout

jig ctx: prints the context size that a tmux session's status line wrote, as tokens over window, and says by its exit code whether the session may start a new step (0 yes, 3 soft limit, 4 hard limit, 2 no reading); run by the orchestrator after each step and by hand; the reading goes to stdout, the limit notes and errors to stderr

jig recompute: runs the scripts in vectors/recompute/ of the -dev clone, then compares vectors/ with the committed tree and the product's vector directory at origin with vectors/, one way, and says by its exit code whether every vector was rebuilt byte for byte (0 yes, 1 a file differs, is new or is missing, 2 not committed, a directory missing or a script failed); run by jig run-check as the row recompute in the specwriter account; the differing paths go to stdout, script output and refusals to stderr

jig trace: in a -dev clone, on its nested product clone. jig trace check checks the trace against the product and the specs (anchors, ID classes, mirrored files, ledger after the import, ID map and the IDs of the pre-import tree), run by make check in the -dev clone and by units; jig trace coverage checks that the records cover each other (owners and control rows of requirements, mutation cells and tests of controls, fixture rows, references of decisions and questions, IDs defined twice), from the records only; jig trace gen <product path> ... adds the entries of the comments that cite IDs to trace/<product path>.json, without touching the product; jig trace form <commit> prints the ledger skeleton of a product commit, one row per function, with <fill> to complete; failures go to stderr, one per line, with the exit code

jig tag: makes an approval tag (spec-pN, spec-p<N>r<M>, impl-pN or kickoff-rN) at a commit of the -dev line that BRANCH names, after its checks (a revision needs a closed review loop for each changed spec document), pushes it and reads it back from origin; run by Eric in a tag block; a refusal goes to stderr in one line, with the exit code

jig changelog: prints the entries of /opt/jig/current/CHANGELOG.md for the versions after the given one; run by the orchestrator at each batch boundary, as jig changelog --since <version>; results go to stdout, errors to stderr

jig upgrade: jig upgrade <version> downloads the GitHub release v<version> with no login, checks each file against its SHA256SUMS, installs the package under /opt/jig/<version>/ and points /opt/jig/current to the newest installed version; jig upgrade <project> <version> installs the version when it is missing, then sets JIG_VERSION in the project's conf file in every role account, and changes no conf file while a lock of the project exists; run by the orchestrator; steps go to stdout, a refusal to stderr

jig terms: jig terms check <project> [<directory>] looks for the private terms of terms.txt in the -dev clone in the paths and contents of the files git lists in the product, in the product commit messages since the last v tag of the line and in the files under <directory>, by their paths below <directory> and their bytes, and prints one line per match with the place and the terms.txt line, never the term; exits 0 with no match, 1 with a match or when it cannot check, 2 on a usage error; run as implementer by jig release prepare and by hand; matches go to stdout, failures to stderr

jig privacy: jig privacy scan <project> scans captures/ and vectors/ of the -dev clone, the product's vector directory and its test files for serials from terms.txt, host names and addresses from the host list, UUIDs, MAC addresses and e-mail addresses, documentation values excepted, and prints one line per match with the place and the kind, never the value; exits 0 with no match, 1 with a match or when it cannot scan, 2 on a usage error; run as implementer by jig release prepare and by hand; matches go to stdout, failures to stderr

jig release: prepare makes the release commit of the line (change log entry, version bump, push), waits for green CI on it, proves it from a clean clone, given the private terms file of the -dev clone, with an offline build of the source archive, checks the release files, the private terms also in the unpacked package, and the privacy scan and every checks.tsv row, and stages the package, the source archive and SHA256SUMS in ~/ws/reviews/<project>/release/<version>/; publish [--dry-run] checks the staged files, the release commit at the head of the line and that master can fast-forward, then tags v<version> in the product and -dev, makes the GitHub release with the staged files, reads it back with no login, and fast-forwards master to the line in both repos with the merge check, and on a rerun acts only on what is missing; verify <version> checks with no login that the published files equal the staged ones, that the tag points at the release commit, that the repo is public and that the CI badge reads passing; run by the implementer unit of a release, prepare as jig release <project> prepare --entry <file> --trailer <line> inside its tmux session, the trailer required; a rerun of prepare reuses and pushes the release commit of an earlier run when nothing in it changed; steps go to stdout, the failed step and its reason to stderr, prepare's command output to ~/ws/reviews/<project>/release/<version>-prepare.txt
